newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chip stocks rocket up 1.48 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chip stocks rocket up 1.48 pct at close.

text.p: Selective Malaysian blue-chip stocks were snapped up in large volumes by foreign institutional investors, equities dealers and analysts said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 17.18 points or 1.48 percent higher at 1175.60, while the all-share EMAS index closed up 3.38 to 337.58.

"The foreign money has been in the market today," said Stephen Weller, director of strategy at Pesaka Jardine Fleming. "There is a growing feeling that U.S. interest rates will not be going up and that the Malaysian macroeconomic picture is improving," he added.
Volumes were sharply up compared to previous sessions. A total of 355.6 million shares changed hands from 289 on Thursday.
Tenaga was up 45 cents at 9.90 ringgit, Proton was up 1.20 ringgit at 15.10, Technology Resources was up 15 cents at 6.45 and Telekom rose 70 at 23.40.

"This is somewhat of a pre-budget rally," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities. "There is anticipation of it being a pro-business budget with goodies for some sectors and with nothing adverse."
Gainers led losers 337 to 224, with 153 stocks unchanged.
"Proton moved up on expectations that their half-year results due out next month will be strong, while TRI moved because it has been a real laggard lately," said Ho.
Proton's closing share price of 15.10 was an all-time high.
"A number of big brokerage houses, including Jardine Fleming and Merrill Lynch, have been on road shows (to promote Malaysian stocks) recently to Europe and the United States," said Ho.
"Much of the foreign funds have been from European and U.S. institutions," said Ami Moris of Capitalcorp Securities.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot October contract was up 17.3 at 1176.3 with 464 lots traded, the November contract was up 17.6 points at 1181.0, with 104 lots traded, and the December contract was up 11 points at 1182.7 with nine lots traded.
Christopher Podbury, executive director at HA Options & Financial Futures said both institutional and retail players were actively buying the futures.

"The considerable strength seen in the futures today, sets the scene for further positive movement in the futures next week. This is supported by the likely emergence of buying interest emanating from speculation as to the contents of the 1997 Budget, to be announced next Friday," he said.
